To me, it was a paradigm shift where I realized how much more is possible when people do things together, and I had to see it happen more. The problem is, every time since then, whether we were buying a group gift or traveling together or buying tickets to a game and actually wanting to sit together, it was the same pain. One person, usually me, had to front the whole cost and then chase people to pay me back one by one. It was awkward, slow, and it strains relationships. The world is designed for solo shopping, so when you hit checkout, you're gonna see a pay now option, you might see a pay later option, but you're almost never gonna see a pay together option, despite the fact that 30% of Gen Z like myself share the cost for something every day. So we built PaySquad to make group payments native at checkout. It's the first buy now, pay together.
